t: Nothing of the King's Bench Prison remains to see. It stood here in Southwark from the Middle Ages until it closed in 1880, and was often used as a debtors' prison. It took its name from the King's Bench court. Several notable people died inside. The novelist Elizabeth Hardy, who published anonymously, died here in 1854, imprisoned for debt after a credulous investment in a joint stock bank. The Scottish spy John Ker died here in 1726, and so did the former governor of Nova Scotia, Samuel Vetch, in 1732.
